guitar.evidence: Adam Jones' silverburst Gibson Les Paul Custom is one of the most recognizable guitars in modern progressive metal.

tone.target: tight low-tuned Tool riff tone with dry mid-harmonic crunch
tone.profile: tight low-tuned Tool riff tone with dry mid-harmonic crunch
tone.summary: A high-gain chain utilizing a distortion pedal (RAT-style) followed by an aggressive amp model (Recti), paired with a 4x12 cabinet to achieve the necessary tight, thick, low-tuned sound with controlled mid-harmonic crunch and subtle filtering.

blocks.purpose: Eliminate hum and noise inherent in high-gain riffing.
Provide initial grit and boost pick attack clarity for tight palm-muting.
blocks.gap: The OD 9 is used as a general dirt/boost, simulating the necessary aggressive edge without adding excessive coloration or fuzz.

blocks.purpose: Add aggressive saturation and mid-harmonic crunch required for Tool's sound.
blocks.gap: The RAT-style provides the necessary tight, biting distortion profile without sounding overly scooped or fuzzy.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the high-gain, aggressive tone of a Mesa/Boogie style amp for low-tuned thickness.
blocks.gap: The Recti model is the closest available option to achieve modern, tight, high-gain metal tones.

blocks.purpose: Provide the necessary physical cabinet simulation for a powerful and defined low-end.
blocks.gap: While not explicitly Mesa/Boogie 4x12, the UK Vintage 4x12 provides sufficient power and definition to support the Recti model's tone.

blocks.purpose: Fine-tune the frequency response to emphasize mid-harmonic crunch and tighten the low end.
Introduce the requested subtle phaser/filter texture without sounding like a full chorus or flanger.
blocks.gap: The T-Wah is used as a general filter sweep to achieve the required 'phaser/filter' effect subtly, avoiding the complexity of dedicated modulation units.

blocks.purpose: Placeholder/Optional: Kept off to avoid the forbidden chorus sound.
Placeholder/Optional: Kept off to avoid big delay.
Provide minimal, natural ambience (dry sound focus).
blocks.gap: Used sparingly to avoid 'lush reverb' while adding necessary depth.

improvements.summary: Upgrade the cabinet IR to better match the Mesa/Boogie aesthetic and enhance low-end definition for tight, aggressive Tool tones.

proposals.reason: Better matches the Mesa/Boogie amp clue and enhances low-end tightness for Tool's signature sound.
proposals.expectedGain: Increased definition and punch in the low end.
